record.paper_title: Initial state fluctuations and final state correlations: Status and open questions
record.original_question: How should the longitudinal direction in fluctuating initial-state profiles be modeled and constrained in 3+1-dimensional viscous hydrodynamic simulations of heavy-ion collisions, given that existing studies of longitudinal fluctuations remain exploratory and η- and Δη-dependent particle correlations may provide useful information?

evidence.quote:
Since
there are more and more 3+1 dimensional (viscous) hydrodynamic codes in use, it is
definitely time to pay more attention to the longitudinal direction. There have been
a few exploratory studies on longitudinal fluctuations [10, 11], but a comprehensive
understanding is still missing. The η and ∆η dependence of particle correlations can
lead to useful insights in that respect.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
In event-by-event 3+1-dimensional viscous relativistic hydrodynamic simulations of high-energy heavy-ion collisions, the initial state is specified at a proper time τ₀ by densities (energy, entropy, conserved charges, and possibly initial flow velocities) on a spacetime-rapidity grid (τ₀, x, y, η_s). Whereas the transverse (x, y)-plane fluctuations have been extensively modeled (e.g. via Glauber-type or saturation-type Monte Carlo prescriptions calibrated to anisotropic flow harmonics v_n), the longitudinal η_s-profile of these fluctuations and their event-by-event correlations across rapidity remain poorly characterized.

Formulate and solve the following modeling/inverse problem:

(a) Construct a parametrization of the fluctuating longitudinal initial-state profile, including correlations between transverse density patterns at different spacetime rapidities (forward–backward asymmetries, longitudinal decorrelation lengths, twist of the event plane with η_s), suitable for input to 3+1D viscous hydrodynamics.

(b) Identify a set of pseudorapidity-dependent final-state observables — in particular, single-particle distributions in pseudorapidity η, two-particle correlations C(η₁, η₂) and their dependence on the rapidity gap Δη, and the η-dependent factorization-breaking ratios r_n(η_a, η_b) of flow harmonics v_n — that quantitatively constrain the parameters introduced in (a).

(c) Determine, through these observables, the longitudinal correlation length and the magnitude of longitudinal fluctuations in the initial condition that are consistent with measured η- and Δη-dependent correlations at RHIC and LHC energies, and assess whether such correlations can uniquely (modulo viscous evolution) fix the longitudinal initial-state model.
artifact.status_search_result: Since 2012, substantial progress has been made: studies of longitudinal decorrelation of v_n via the r_n(η_a,η_b) observable (CMS, ATLAS) and 3+1D hydrodynamic models (CLVisc, AMPT-initialized hydro, McDIPPER, sub-nucleonic fluctuating initial states) have constrained longitudinal fluctuation profiles. However, a fully comprehensive, uniquely-constrained model of longitudinal initial-state fluctuations is still under active development; the program is partially solved rather than complete.

status_evidence.title: Longitudinal fluctuations and decorrelation of anisotropic flow
status_evidence.snippet: Decorrelation of 2nd and 3rd order flow studied across η gaps in event-by-event (3+1)D hydrodynamics with AMPT initial conditions; decorrelation traced to spatial decorrelation along the longitudinal direction.
status_evidence.claim: Subsequent works have begun to model and constrain longitudinal initial-state fluctuations using η-gap-dependent flow correlations.

status_evidence.title: Effects of sub-nucleonic fluctuations on the longitudinal structure of heavy-ion collisions
status_evidence.snippet: Sub-nucleonic initial-state fluctuations affect longitudinal decorrelation observables in 3+1D viscous hydrodynamics (CLVisc).
status_evidence.claim: Active progress continues on modeling longitudinal initial-state fluctuations within 3+1D viscous hydrodynamics.

status_evidence.title: McDIPPER: A 3+1D initial-state model for heavy ion collisions
status_evidence.snippet: Saturation-based rapidity-resolved Monte Carlo initial-state generator depositing conserved charges across rapidity.
status_evidence.claim: New rapidity-resolved initial-state models address the longitudinal direction explicitly.
